parsed.why: Strong rule of law, self-ID, hate-crime recourse and broad acceptance, but documented airport-screening degradation and binary prison placement (legally female prisoner sent to men's unit) remain traveller-facing exposures; sauna access left to operators.

State threat-framing plus universal-exposure border measures: markers forced to birth sex, case-note tagging, fraud ineligibility risk, advisories from eight governments; bathroom bans across many states with a documented arrest held in a men's ward.

No gender-identity law, police refusal in anti-LGBT death investigations, and state custody abuse of trans women (forced shaving, punishment drills, care denial) with one still imprisoned; single hate-crime conviction does not offset documented impunity.

Decriminalisation upheld, functioning courts, harassment law naming gender identity; but thin data on prison, border and screening, an immigration provision naming homosexuals (narrowly interpreted), and no trans-specific recourse — a step below acceptance-with-protections.

Statutory gender-identity protections and hate-crime law, but enforcement fails: trans woman denied service, arson uninvestigated, hate speech unaddressed, very low acceptance (79% reject neighbours), and a trans detainee isolated and humiliated in custody.
